sources.citation: Killian, Don & Russell Barlow. 2022. Deictic marking in adpositions in Ap Ma and Waran. Linguistic Typology at the Crossroads 2(1): 37-64. doi:10.6092/issn.2785-0943/13575
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Discusses prosody only in the sense of phonological-word formation: postpositions are enclitics needing proclitic hosts (p. 45), and 'semi-free nouns' (pa 'house', mi 'water' etc.) are vowel-final monosyllables that are 'phonologically bound to the following word or suffix and can never occur in isolation' (pp. 56-57, quoting Wade 1983b: 3-4).

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2021. Ambakich phonological sketch. Language and Linguistics in Oceania 13: 32-88.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is 'mainly concerned with segmental phonology'; it gives the Ap Ma phoneme inventory (p. 36: /p, t, k, mb, nd, ŋg, ndʒ, m, n, (ɲ), (ŋ), l, s, w, j, i, ɨ, u, e, o, ɐ/, Yamen village data) and a 602-item Ap Ma word list (pp. 71-88), but the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the article and no stress marks are given in the Ap Ma or Ambakich word lists. Only prosodic remark (p. 71): vowel-final monosyllabic words are disfavored at the end of prosodic units, so citation forms are given with the focus suffix -ndɨma.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2020. A sketch grammar of Pondi. Canberra: ANU Press (Asia-Pacific Linguistics).
sources.note: Nothing about Ap Ma stress. Ap Ma appears only in the Keram comparative section (pp. 14-17: pronouns, TAM forms from Wade 1984, ~20% cognacy with Ulmapo). §2.4 p. 35 ('Stress in Pondi is not phonemic.. slight preference for penultimate (trochaic) stress') concerns Pondi, not Ap Ma.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In A. Pawley, R. Attenborough, J. Golson & R. Hide (eds), Papuan pasts, 109-144. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 572.
sources.note: Nothing. Kambot is discussed only for classification (rejects Laycock & Z'graggen's Grass family; treats Kambot as an isolated first-order member of Lower Sepik-Ramu); sources listed for Kambot are Laycock (1959) and Pryor (1990).

Kambot sketch pp. 758-760 gives only a phoneme list (/p t s k b d j g v r m n ŋ w y a e i o u ai/, prenasalised voiced stops, p/v and t/r neutralisation), pronouns, the -dama suffix on monosyllabic nouns, verb suffixes and SOV order; no mention of stress, tone or pitch anywhere in the chapter.
